answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring every identity to accumulate a verified record of work before its voice gains weight. A newcomer starts on open tundra: nothing is granted, so it must contribute checkable labor and gather countersignatures from established peers before its vote counts. Reputation is a velvet surface that only deepens with corroboration, while a pulse of fresh keys carries no history behind it. Because influence follows witnessed tenure rather than account count, a farm spawning a thousand identities gets a thousand silent shells, as empty as a walnut husk.
